_comment: Accepted content-validation findings (spec content-validation §4.3). One entry per finding, or per finding class via identityPattern, each with a reason. A stale entry (matching no finding) fails ContentStructureTest.

entries.reason: extra_simultaneous_wall_constructions is the legacy per-level field the converter emits; the loader reads a plan-set-scope extra_wall_construction_slots that nothing emits, so the value is silently 0 today. Code defect (WallGrowthManager.computeMaxSlots reads the plan set, legacy Building.getSimultaneousWallConstructionSlots read the building's current level plan) recorded in the 2026-09 baseline — the content is right, the loader is not. Remove this entry when the loader reads the level field.

Templates with no path start, selling or sleeping position: lone ruins and abandoned sites, player fields, caves and inuksuit — none has residents or a counter to path to. Legacy skipped such templates silently; the rewrite's FallbackAnchorFinder probes the perimeter and logs it (documented deviation). Adding a marker is a per-template editorial decision, not a defect fix.

Sub-buildings whose parent does not list them back: the eight legacy asymmetries pinned in JarPlanCoherenceTest.everyShippedSubHasValidParentRef (geometry-source parents that never spawn the sub — verified against the 1.12 .txt corpus). The message fragment is deliberate: CultureLoader.checkSubBuildingParentRef emits a second, distinct diagnostic on the same plan sets ('footprint of parent building plan … does not match that of the sub-building'), which this entry must not swallow — that one is a real geometry defect, not an accepted asymmetry.

The miner carries mine_sand as in 1.12 (indian_miner.txt: goal=minesand) but no indian or mayan building template in 9.x carries a sand mock_source (reachable: sandstone, red_sandstone, stone). Either the legacy PNG source was lost in conversion (GH-325 class) or legacy tolerated the idle goal; which building should carry the source is an owner decision recorded in the 2026-09 baseline. The eleven village types are enumerated rather than matched by '(indian|mayan)/villages/.*' so that a village type added later to either culture is a new finding someone has to decide on, not a silently accepted one.

The Japanese lone mine's villagers carry mine_gravel but the lonemine template exposes clay, sandstone and stone sources only. Owner decision recorded in the 2026-09 baseline (GH-326 wired the extra mine_* goals; the source side was not revisited).

The sanduit lone building's villagers carry the inuit ice/snow mining goals (buildingTag inuitmining) but no inuitmining-tagged building of that village type carries a mock_source. Owner decision recorded in the 2026-09 baseline.
